title: TCP & UDP Transport Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision of TCP connection setup and teardown, sequence/ACK numbering, flow and congestion control, UDP trade-offs, and how ports and sockets identify endpoints.

chapters.title: Transport Layer Mental Model: Ports, Sockets, TCP vs UDP
points: Transport layer gives process-to-process delivery; IP gives host-to-host delivery
Port is a 16-bit number (0-65535): well-known 0-1023, registered 1024-49151, ephemeral 49152-65535
Socket = IP address + port; a TCP connection is uniquely identified by the 4-tuple (src IP, src port, dst IP, dst port)
One listening port can serve many clients because each connection has a different 4-tuple
TCP: connection-oriented, reliable, ordered byte stream; UDP: connectionless, unreliable datagrams

chapters.title: TCP Handshake and Teardown
points: Three-way handshake: client SYN (seq=x) → server SYN-ACK (seq=y, ack=x+1) → client ACK (ack=y+1)
SYN and FIN each consume one sequence number even with no data
Teardown is four steps: FIN → ACK → FIN → ACK, because each direction closes independently (half-close)
Active closer enters TIME_WAIT for 2×MSL (about 60s) so late packets expire and the final ACK can be resent
RST aborts a connection immediately, sent when a segment arrives for a closed port or on a fatal error

chapters.title: Sequence Numbers and ACKs
points: Sequence number is the byte offset of the first data byte in the segment, not a segment counter
ACK number = next byte the receiver expects (cumulative acknowledgement)
Example: segment seq=1000 carrying 500 bytes → receiver replies ack=1500
Initial sequence number (ISN) is random per connection to avoid stale-packet confusion and spoofing
Three duplicate ACKs trigger fast retransmit without waiting for the retransmission timeout (RTO)

chapters.title: Flow Control: Sliding Window
points: Flow control protects the receiver; the receiver advertises its free buffer as rwnd in every ACK
Sender may have at most min(rwnd, cwnd) unacknowledged bytes in flight
Window slides right as ACKs arrive, allowing new bytes to be sent
rwnd = 0 stalls the sender; it sends zero-window probes until the receiver reopens the window
Window scaling option (up to 2^14 shift) is needed to exceed 65535-byte window on high bandwidth-delay links

chapters.title: Congestion Control: Slow Start and AIMD
points: Congestion control protects the network; the sender keeps its own cwnd, flow control protects the receiver
Slow start: cwnd starts at about 10 MSS and doubles every RTT until it reaches ssthresh
Congestion avoidance (AIMD): add about 1 MSS per RTT (additive increase)
On loss, multiplicative decrease: ssthresh = cwnd/2
Timeout drops cwnd to 1 MSS and restarts slow start; 3 duplicate ACKs (Reno) halve cwnd and continue in fast recovery
Common mistake: confusing rwnd (receiver limit) with cwnd (network limit)

chapters.title: TCP vs UDP Cheat Sheet
points: UDP header is 8 bytes (src port, dst port, length, checksum); TCP header is at least 20 bytes
Use UDP for DNS, VoIP, video streaming, games, DHCP and QUIC: low latency matters and loss is tolerable or handled by the app
Use TCP for HTTP/1-2, SSH, SMTP and file transfer: need reliability and ordering
Inspect sockets: ss -tan (TCP states), ss -ulpn (UDP listeners), nc -zv host port (port check)
Common error: 'Address already in use' means the port is bound or in TIME_WAIT; use SO_REUSEADDR for servers
Quick recall: handshake SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK, ACK = next expected byte, window = min(rwnd, cwnd), slow start doubles then AIMD
